$comment: MCP-style tool definitions for every content API endpoint. dynamic/silverstripe-content-api-mcp maps one tool per entry onto the REST endpoint, injecting the X-Silverstripe-Apitoken header. Class payload contracts are discovered at runtime via the schema_class tool.

tools.name: content_auth_session
tools.description: Verify the current API token: member, held permissions, expiry.

tools.name: content_schema_site
tools.description: Discover the site's content API surface: exposed classes with verbs/capabilities, detected integrations (elemental, linkfield, Essentials palette + button labels), environment and whether population endpoints are enabled. Call this first. Check the response's populationEnabled field before a first batch/composition/asset/page-action write against a target you haven't written to before — a passing dev/test rehearsal never exercises the population environment gate, so it gives no warning that a live/uat target will 403 ENV_FORBIDDEN until you actually hit it there.

tools.name: content_schema_class
tools.description: Get one class's payload contract: fields with types/writability/enum values/token hints, honesty flags (computed: recomputed by the model on save; importOwned: owned by an external feed — both advisory, writes land but are silently overwritten) with an optional note, has_one payload kinds (assetRef|link|recordRef), has_many/many_many writability and, when the relation carries extra join data (a classic many_many_extraFields map or a many_many through join class), an extraFields array naming those fields before you round-trip {"id", "extraFields"} items.

tools.name: content_records_list
tools.description: List records of a class with filtering (Field=value, Field__PartialMatch etc.), sorting (-Field for DESC), pagination and stage selection.

filters.description: Field or Field__Modifier keys; modifiers: ExactMatch, PartialMatch, StartsWith, EndsWith, GreaterThan(OrEqual), LessThan(OrEqual), not, nocase, case

tools.name: content_records_read
tools.description: Read one record by numeric id or external id (ext: prefix). Returns fields (PascalCase, round-trips into writes), relation ids (a many_many with extraFields returns {id, extraFields} per item instead of a bare id) and draft/live stage state.

tools.name: content_records_parity
tools.description: Does this record, and everything it $owns, match between draft and live, and where do they differ. Compares a configurable set of the root's own fields (Title/ParentID/ClassName/ShowInMenus/URLSegment/Sort by default, filtered to whichever the class actually declares) draft vs live — the record not existing on live at all is reported as liveExists: false, a legitimate state, not a failure. Also walks the record's $owns tree recursively (include=none to skip; depth=N to cap it, rejecting a non-numeric value rather than silently disabling the walk) reporting each owned descendant's live/draft status and depth (not a field-level diff — only the root gets that). An owned descendant's live status disagreeing with the root's own is a mismatch (ok: false) either direction: root live + descendant draft-only, or root not-live + descendant live (stranded content); root and descendant agreeing, live or not, is consistent. Both the root and every owned record are read by their true base class, not a narrower requested/concrete class, so a record converted to a different class on draft only still reports its live row correctly (the class difference itself surfaces as an ordinary ClassName field mismatch). Response carries both a machine-readable structure (fields/owned/liveExists/ok) and a flat report: [{label, ok, message}] list. 400 PAYLOAD_INVALID for a non-Versioned class — nothing to compare.

depth.description: Caps how far the $owns walk recurses. Unset uses the module's configured default.

tools.name: content_fingerprint
tools.description: A deterministic, path-keyed snapshot of the site's content for diffing across gates (before/after a batch) or environments (a local rehearsal vs. production). Pages are keyed by their URL path, not id — ids churn across a rebuild/sync/environment boundary, paths don't (call with includeIds=true to add ids back for debugging a specific row, but don't diff on them). Also asserts the reachability invariant a plain snapshot can't: violations lists every live page (or live related record) whose path runs through a non-live ancestor, since SiteTree::get_by_link() 404s on the first non-live path segment regardless of the target row's own live status; duplicate violations describing one shared blocked owner page collapse to one. related sections (project-configured, e.g. a hero-image relation keyed by its owning page's FK column) report unresolved counts for owners that don't resolve to a known page rather than leaking a raw id into records (includeIds=true surfaces a separate unresolvedIds list instead). classes restricts which sections appear in the response (pages plus any configured related ref) without breaking owner-path resolution for the sections that are still requested, and never restricts violations itself — a reachability problem is always reported even when its own section is excluded from the response, and an unrecognized ref is rejected (400 PAYLOAD_INVALID) rather than silently producing an empty section. Applies the same class- and record-level access control as every other read endpoint, per row: a class not exposed to the content API at all appears in meta.skipped (site-wide, not per-caller); a class that IS exposed but a specific row this token can't view (e.g. a draft-only page without VIEW_DRAFT_CONTENT) is simply absent from the response rather than disclosed, and totals (per section, draft/live counts) reflect only what this token can see.

classes.description: Comma-separated section refs to include ("pages" plus any configured related ref). Omit to include every section.

includeIds.description: Add each row's numeric id. Off by default — the whole point of this snapshot is being diffable across environments where ids aren't stable.

tools.name: content_records_stage
tools.description: Publish, unpublish or archive a record. Response reports resulting draft/live state. unpublish refuses (409 UNPUBLISH_STRANDS_DESCENDANTS) if the record has any live Hierarchy descendants; archive refuses if it has any in either stage (SiteTree.enforce_strict_hierarchy cascades a delete to every current child in the stage(s) being deleted from) — move/publish them elsewhere first, or pass force to proceed anyway and accept the loss. mode=subtree authorization-checks every descendant it would touch before writing anything (403 FORBIDDEN_CLASS/FORBIDDEN_RECORD on the first one the caller can't publish, nothing written on refusal); pass liveOnly=true to skip a descendant branch entirely (no publish, no recursing into it) when it isn't already live, or dryRun=true to preview the would-publish set (same authorization checks, no writes) instead of the normal response. liveOnly/dryRun are 400 PAYLOAD_INVALID on any mode other than subtree. A real (non-dryRun) subtree call keeps the normal response but adds meta.published: the same [{id, className}, ...] list dryRun previews, so a liveOnly call still reports what was actually touched.

mode.description: publish only: takes precedence over the legacy recursive boolean below. subtree publishes the record then every draft Hierarchy child depth-first — the way to publish a moved subtree before unpublishing its old wrapper, see the descendant-cascade guard above.

recursive.description: publish only: legacy shorthand for mode=recursive, kept for backward compatibility. Ignored when mode is present.

force.description: unpublish/archive only: bypass the descendant-cascade guard

liveOnly.description: mode=subtree only, 400 PAYLOAD_INVALID otherwise: skip a descendant branch entirely (no publish, no recursing into its own children) when it isn't already live — prevents resurrecting a page deliberately taken offline just because a live ancestor is being restructured

dryRun.description: mode=subtree only, 400 PAYLOAD_INVALID otherwise: run the full authorization-checked walk and return the would-publish set without writing anything

tools.name: content_batch
tools.description: Run ordered write operations with per-op results and a summary (agent self-correction contract). atomic=true wraps a transaction and rolls everything back on first failure. On atomic failure, a rolledBack: true result is independently verified before it's reported — every 'created', 'deleted' (whose mode could actually have reached the draft row: archive, or any mode on an unversioned class; unpublish on a versioned class only touches live, so it's correctly skipped), and 'updated' (its declared fields, re-checked against a pre-write snapshot) op is re-checked — an unverified rollback reports 500 ROLLBACK_UNVERIFIED instead, carrying the same results array so every entry can be checked by hand. dryRun=true runs the batch exactly as a real request would (same authorization/resolution/validation) inside a transaction that's unconditionally rolled back afterward, regardless of atomic or outcome. On success (or a predicted atomic failure) every status in the response is prefixed 'would' (wouldCreate/wouldUpdate/wouldDelete) so it can never be mistaken for a confirmed write; a dry run that itself can't be verified as zero-persistence reports 500 ROLLBACK_UNVERIFIED with real (unmapped) verbs instead, since at that point the caller genuinely can't tell whether it committed. Supported on this endpoint only, rejected elsewhere. Attaching an element to a page whose Elemental config doesn't permit that type fails that op with 422 ELEMENT_NOT_ALLOWED_ON_PAGE.

dryRun.description: Validate and authorize every operation, then unconditionally roll back — nothing is ever persisted. Response statuses are prefixed 'would' (wouldCreate/wouldUpdate/wouldDelete) on success; a 500 ROLLBACK_UNVERIFIED failure uses real (unmapped) verbs instead.

relations.description: has_one writes: bare id/externalId for a normal relation; a polymorphic has_one (no single target class) rejects a bare id and requires {"class": "...", "id": n} or {"class": "...", "externalId": "..."} — see content_schema_class for which relations are polymorphic

force.description: delete op with mode=unpublish or mode=archive only: bypass the descendant-cascade guard

tools.name: content_compose_page
tools.description: Compose a full page atomically: match/create/convert the page, upsert ordered elements (array order = Sort) with children/relations/link payloads/color tokens, ingest assets with $ref aliases, optionally prune managed elements missing from the payload, publish everything explicitly. Re-POSTing the same payload is idempotent (updates, never duplicates). Any failure rolls the whole request back. An element type the target page's Elemental config (allowed_elements/disallowed_elements) doesn't permit is rejected with 422 ELEMENT_NOT_ALLOWED_ON_PAGE, listing the page's actual allowed types — same check the CMS's own "add element" picker uses.

force.description: Required to convert the site home page

ref.description: Per-request alias usable as {"$ref": …} in element fields

children.description: hasManyRelation: [{externalId, fields, class?}] — owned records under the element's aggregate

relations.description: has_one writes: bare id/externalId for a normal relation; a polymorphic has_one (no single target class) rejects a bare id and requires {"class": "...", "id": n} or {"class": "...", "externalId": "..."} — see content_schema_class for which relations are polymorphic

tools.name: content_asset_upload
tools.description: Upload a file into the asset store with folder placement. Identical content is hash-skipped but ALWAYS returns the full record (existed=true) so relations can be wired on every run. Provide exactly one of "base64" or "filePath" — an MCP client resolves "filePath" locally (on the machine running the MCP host) and never sends the path itself over HTTP, so a caller with only a local file path never has to inline a large binary through its own context.

base64.description: Base64-encoded file content. Mutually exclusive with filePath.

filePath.description: Absolute path to a local file, read and base64-encoded by the MCP client before the request is sent — the upstream API never sees this field. Mutually exclusive with base64. Not applicable to a direct HTTP caller (curl etc.), which must send base64 itself.

tools.name: content_asset_read
tools.description: Read one asset (numeric id or ext:) with url, hash and filename.

tools.name: content_page_convert
tools.description: Change a page's class via newClassInstance (e.g. Page → BlockPage). Refuses the site home page without force=true.

tools.name: content_page_apply_template
tools.description: Apply an elemental-templates Template's element composition to a page (requires dynamic/silverstripe-elemental-templates).

genericCrud.note: Generic CRUD: GET/POST/PUT/DELETE api/$Model(/$ID) with the same token. Stage-unaware (writes land unpublished on the current stage; no _stage, no ext:). Discover model refs via content_schema_site .crud.models. Auth: POST api/auth/login with email/pwd request vars.
